title: ChIP on BJ infected by HSV-1
author: Patrick Lomonte
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wjafcie

steps.title: Crosslink cells with formaldehyde
steps.instruction: Add 16 % methanol‑free formaldehyde to the culture medium to a final concentration of 1 % and incubate 5 min at room temperature on a shaking platform.

steps.title: Quench crosslinking with glycine
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of 2.5 M glycine to the fixed cells, incubate 5 min at room temperature, then aspirate the solution completely.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL cold PBS to each dish, scrape the cells, add additional cold PBS to collect any remaining cells, then centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C (speed may be adjusted for cell type).

steps.title: Wash cells with protease inhibitors
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in cold PBS containing 1× protease inhibitor cocktail (PIC), centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C; repeat the wash once more.

steps.title: Lyse cells and isolate nuclei
steps.instruction: Add 1× Lysis Buffer containing 1× PIC, gently resuspend, incubate 10 min on a rocker at 4 °C, then centrifuge at 1,700 g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash nuclei and repeat wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclear pellet in 1× Wash Buffer with 1× PIC, incubate 10 min on a rocker at 4 °C, centrifuge at 1,700 g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant; repeat this wash once more.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei and shear chromatin
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 1× Shearing Buffer with 1× PIC, transfer to 1 mL AFA tube(s), and shear using an S220 focused ultrasonicator at 140 W, 10 % duty cycle, burst mode 200 cycles.

steps.title: Dilute chromatin and clear debris
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 2× IP Buffer to the sonicated sample, mix, then centrifuge at 16,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C; transfer the supernatant to a new tube and set aside 10 % as input (snap‑freeze at –80 °C if not used immediately).

steps.title: Immunoprecipitation overnight
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate primary antibody (or IgG control) to each cleared chromatin sample and rotate at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Add protein G/A beads
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL protein G or A agarose beads (pre‑blocked with salmon sperm DNA, Millipore) to each sample and rotate at 4 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Collect bead‑chromatin complexes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the IP samples at 100 g for 30 s at 4 °C, discard the supernatant, then gently pellet the beads by centrifugation at 700–1,000 rpm for 1 min at 4 °C and remove the remaining supernatant.

steps.title: Wash immunoprecipitated complexes
steps.instruction: Sequentially wash the bead complexes on a rotating platform for 3–5 min each with 1 mL of the following buffers: (a) 1× Low Salt Buffer, (b) 1× High Salt Buffer, (c) 1× Low Salt Buffer (wash), (d) 2× LiCl Buffer, (e) 1× Low Salt Buffer (wash), (f) 1× TE.

steps.title: Elute DNA‑protein complexes
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL elution buffer to the beads, incubate at 65 °C for 30 min with rotation, spin briefly, and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.

steps.title: RNase A and proteinase K treatment
steps.instruction: To each IP and input sample add 2.5 µL RNase A (20 mg/mL stock, final 0.2 mg/mL) and 2.5 µL proteinase K (20 mg/mL stock, final 0.2 mg/mL); incubate at 65 °C overnight.

steps.title: Purify DNA
steps.instruction: Recover DNA from the eluates by phenol/chloroform extraction or using a PCR clean‑up kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
